chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Humayd ibn al-Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sam'a, from more than one, from Aban ibn 'Uthman, from Hammad ibn Bashir, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:

Whoever drinks wine after Allah made it forbidden on my tongue is not worthy of being married if he proposes, nor believed if he narrates, nor interceded for if he intercedes, nor trusted with a trust. And whoever entrusts him with a trust and he consumes it or loses it, the one who entrusted him will not be rewarded by Allah nor compensated for it.

Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: I intended to entrust merchandise to someone to take to Yemen, so I went to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and said: I intend to entrust so-and-so. He said: Do you not know that he drinks wine? I said: It reached me from the believers that they say that. He said: Believe them, for indeed Allah, Exalted and Majestic, says: 'He believes in Allah and believes in the believers.'

Then he said: If you entrust him and it perishes or is lost, you will not be rewarded by Allah nor compensated for it. So I entrusted him and he lost it, so I supplicated to Allah, Exalted and Majestic, that He reward me. He said: O my son, stop. You are not rewarded by Allah nor compensated for it.

I said: Why? He said: Because Allah, Exalted and Majestic, says: 'And do not give the foolish your wealth which Allah has made for you a means of support.' Do you know a more foolish person than the drinker of wine?

And he said: The servant remains in a spaciousness (ease) from Allah, Exalted and Majestic, until he drinks wine. When he drinks it, Allah strips his garment from him, and his patron and his brother becomes Iblis, and his hearing, sight, hand, and foot drive him to every evil and turn him away from every good.

key_terms.يُزَوَّجَ: To be married off (in the context of suitability)

ai.seo_question: What are the legal and social consequences for a person who drinks wine according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the jurisprudential principle that habitual wine consumption renders a person *safiha* (foolish/impulsive), thereby invalidating their financial reliability (*amanah*) and social credibility. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) illustrates this by entrusting merchandise to a drinker, citing Quran 4:5 to demonstrate that their inherent foolishness justifies the loss of capital without divine compensation, a concept further reinforced by the narrative of the garment being 'torn' to signify spiritual exposure and the shift of guardianship to Iblis.
